animation.sequence.summary: Plan a deterministic presentation timeline over declared tracks (camera, visibility, section, joint, occurrence) with an easing law, timing and fps, producing a frame manifest. Read-only: nothing is mutated and no native storyboard action is authored.

inputs.tracks: Nonempty array of typed tracks: camera {from:{eye,target,up},to:{eye,target,up}}; visibility {ref,visible:bool}; section {name,isLightBulbOn:bool}; joint {ref,rotation?{from,to},slide?{from,to}}; occurrence {ref,axis,distance}. Each may declare a phase.
inputs.phases: Optional ordered phase names (equal time slices). Tracks without a phase join the last phase.
inputs.duration: Required positive total duration in seconds.
inputs.fps: Required positive integer frames per second.
inputs.easing: Optional one of linear, smoothstep, easeIn, easeOut, easeInOut; default linear.

limitations: Deterministic evaluated frame manifest, not a native storyboard action sequence. Camera/visibility/section values are plan data, not a rendered-view equivalence proof. Continuous tracks ease within their phase; discrete visibility/section steps apply at their phase start.

animation.export.summary: Encode already-rendered frame files into a film through a declared encoder. With no declared (or unavailable) encoder the result is blocked and no fake video file is written. ffmpeg uses a concat template producing a genuinely playable mp4.

inputs.frames: Nonempty array of existing .png frame paths on the Fusion machine (CLI maps WSL/native paths).
inputs.output: Nonempty film path; must not already exist. Parent directory must exist.
inputs.encoder: Optional {name, program?, arguments?} or {name, command:[argv...]}. name 'ffmpeg' uses a concat template; other names append frames + output to the declared argv. Omitted or unavailable -> blocked, no file written.
inputs.fps: Optional positive integer; required for the ffmpeg concat template and reported as provenance.
inputs.confirm: Must be true; writes a file.

limitations: Without a declared (and runnable) encoder no film file is written; a fake or empty video is never produced. The encoder runs on the Fusion machine. Output is verified nonempty but not transcoded/validated byte-for-byte here.
